common_name: Siloam Royal Prince Daylily (Red-Purple Self Siloam Series)

planting.note: Plant dormant-foliage divisions in spring or early fall in well-drained soil in full sun; this diploid Siloam-series introduction from Pauline Henry forms a dense clump of ruffled, wide-petaled blooms and multiplies readily once established.

directions: Bred by Pauline Henry of Siloam Springs, Arkansas, this diploid daylily carries a deep red-purple self-colored flower with a faint white midrib and a contrasting chartreuse-green throat on scapes that rise above the foliage in midseason. The dormant clump bulks up quickly in average garden soil and rewards division every three to four years with a heavier bud count. Plant in full sun for the richest color saturation and deadhead spent scapes to keep the bed tidy through the bloom season.

common_name: Siloam Doodlebug Daylily (Miniature Eyed Siloam Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; a compact miniature-flowered Siloam-series diploid bred by Pauline Henry that suits edging and small-space plantings.

directions: Bred by Pauline Henry, Siloam Doodlebug produces small, icy lemon-yellow blooms under three inches across, each marked with a sharp black-purple eyezone and a green throat, on compact scapes that flower early to midseason. Its diminutive, well-proportioned flowers qualify it for the miniature show classification and make it a good choice for the front of a border or a daylily collector's rock garden bed. The dormant clump is tough and easy, needing only average soil, full sun, and division every few years to stay vigorous.

common_name: Siloam Shocker Daylily (Pink and Crimson-Eyed Siloam Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; this extended-bloom-habit Siloam-series diploid from Pauline Henry holds its flowers open later into the afternoon than many older daylilies.

directions: Pauline Henry named Siloam Shocker for the vivid contrast between its blush-pink petals and the crimson-red eyezone banding each flower above a dark green throat. The scapes run taller than many of Henry's Siloam introductions, carrying blooms with an extended flowering habit well above the dormant foliage clump during the midseason flush. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil and divide congested clumps every three to four years to maintain strong bud counts.

common_name: Siloam Purple Plum Daylily (Dark Purple Self Siloam Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; a Pauline Henry Siloam-series introduction with a compact, early-to-midseason habit and extended bloom.

directions: Siloam Purple Plum bears a dark red-purple self flower with a cool green throat on a compact, early-to-midseason scape with an extended bloom habit, one of the darker-toned introductions in Pauline Henry's long-running Siloam breeding line. It forms a tidy dormant clump that is easy to grow in average garden soil and benefits from division every three to four years. Plant in full sun for the deepest color and divide congested clumps to keep bud counts high.

common_name: Siloam Little Girl Daylily (Shrimp Pink Siloam Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; a Pauline Henry Siloam-series diploid with a soft shrimp-pink bloom suited to cottage-style perennial borders.

directions: Siloam Little Girl produces soft shrimp-pink flowers banded with a rosy eyezone and finished with a green-gold throat, opening on proportionate scapes during the midseason flush. The dormant foliage clump stays compact and well-mannered, making it a good fit for mixed perennial borders where a pastel-toned daylily is wanted without an oversized footprint. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil and divide every few years to keep bloom counts high.

common_name: Siloam Satin Daylily (Pink Self Siloam Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; an early diploid introduction in Pauline Henry's Siloam breeding line.

directions: Siloam Satin carries a large, pink self-colored flower with a small gold throat on tall scapes that open during the midseason bloom window, an early diploid in Pauline Henry's decades-long Siloam breeding program based in Siloam Springs, Arkansas. It grows easily in average, well-drained soil in full sun and divides readily in spring or fall. As an early Siloam introduction it is historically notable as a foundation plant behind many later, more heavily patterned cultivars in the line.

common_name: Siloam Splendor Daylily (Apricot Blend Siloam Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; an early apricot-blend introduction in Pauline Henry's Siloam breeding line.

directions: Siloam Splendor carries large, warm apricot-blend flowers set off by a clean green throat, opening on tall, well-proportioned scapes during the midseason bloom flush, part of Pauline Henry's long-running Siloam breeding line out of Siloam Springs, Arkansas. The dormant clump is vigorous and easy to grow in average garden soil, making it a reliable addition to a daylily collection. Divide every three to four years in spring or fall to maintain strong flowering.

common_name: Siloam Plum Tree Daylily (Deep Purple Self Siloam Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; a Pauline Henry Siloam-series diploid with a saturated purple self flower.

directions: Siloam Plum Tree carries a deep, saturated purple self-colored flower with a clean green throat that opens early to midseason on well-proportioned scapes, one of the darker-toned Siloam introductions from Pauline Henry. The strong, dark color and dormant, vigorous clump habit have made it a lasting favorite among growers who collect the darker-toned Siloam cultivars. It performs reliably in average, well-drained soil in full sun and benefits from division every three to four years as the clump thickens.

common_name: Siloam Red Toy Daylily (Small-Flowered Red Siloam Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; a Pauline Henry Siloam-series introduction with a compact, small-flowered red bloom.

directions: Siloam Red Toy bears a compact, saturated red self flower under three inches across with a contrasting green throat, opening early to midseason on scapes proportioned to the small bloom size. The dormant clump is easy-care and multiplies steadily in average, well-drained soil, making it a good choice for a border planting of small-flowered Siloam-series cultivars from Pauline Henry's breeding line. Divide every few years to maintain strong bud counts.

common_name: Siloam Button Box Daylily (Cream and Maroon-Eyed Siloam Series)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; a Pauline Henry Siloam-series diploid with a cream ground and a contrasting maroon eyezone.

directions: Siloam Button Box has a neat, buttoned-up flower form: a cream ground banded with a maroon eyezone and finished with a green throat, opening early to midseason on well-branched scapes. Its wide, substantial petals and clear color contrast have kept it in circulation among Siloam-series collectors long after many contemporaries faded from commerce. The dormant clump grows readily in average, well-drained soil in full sun and divides easily every three to four years.
